scope.summary: Resolve the operations/identity/workflow founder-call gate by reconciling BVB-06/BVB-07/BVB-08 to current accepted founder/current authorities and queueing ADR prose follow-up work.
explicit_non_claims: No product code, runtime service, OIDC provider, Workflow engine, DCIM, or silicon implementation is changed.
The portfolio ownership-ratchet gate remains planned; this change does not claim mechanical enforcement behind oya-ci-required.
The source ADR prose still needs a separate docs amendment lane where older wording conflicts; this task queues that follow-up rather than silently editing every ADR.
No OWN_DAY0 developer-portal claim is introduced by this reconciliation; the resolution only separates Internal Developer Platform portal/BFF wording from OIDC identity-provider authority.
The reconciled identity outcome is a founder-accepted bridge-plus-bespoke roadmap, not an implication of the Internal Developer Platform naming collision.

hyperscaler_lens.north_star: Own differentiating substrates with explicit bridge discipline, parity gates, and founder authority instead of letting old day-0 ownership language create unbounded simultaneous substrate programs.
hyperscaler_lens.scale_property: Workflow stays behind a Temporal-class bridge until Tier-3 durable-execution parity, DCIM waits for physical/colo DC capacity and silicon founder-ratification, while identity follows the explicit ADR-0476/ADR-0482 bridge-plus-bespoke roadmap.

facets.F1_correctness: BVB-06, BVB-07, and BVB-08 now have explicit resolved default buckets, resolution authorities, and founder_call_required=false in the ratchet mapping.
facets.F2_tests: JSON syntax validation, custom BVB invariant validation, git diff --check, and Kanban follow-up creation are required verification evidence for this slice.
facets.F3_maintainability: The decisions are kept in one machine-readable mapping with separate ADR amendment work queued for older prose conflicts.
facets.F4_compatibility: The change is additive to metadata fields on an existing proposed architecture-governance spec and does not touch generated faces or runtime APIs.
facets.F5_security: Identity-provider ownership is tied to ADR-0476 feature parity and security/privacy review evidence instead of being inferred from portal wording.
facets.F6_privacy: No tenant, customer, employee, or credential data is introduced; the artifact contains architecture metadata only.
facets.F7_operability: The blocked human-only card can close because accepted source authority now records the decision buckets; follow-up ADR amendments are visible as t_ec29b160.
facets.F8_performance: No runtime path is affected; future engines remain behind parity/bridge gates before any performance claim.
facets.F9_compliance: DCIM and silicon wording preserves founder-ratified high-blast-radius gates and avoids unsupported regulated-operations ownership claims.
facets.F10_reversibility: Rollback is limited to the ratchet JSON diff, this evidence file, and the Kanban follow-up card/comment.
facets.F11_observability: The Kanban board records the resolution and the follow-up docs amendment card for traceability.
facets.F13_migration: The follow-up lane migrates ADR prose from older day-0/vendor defaults to the accepted bridge-plus-bespoke roadmap without mixing it into this decision gate.

decision_resolutions.resolution: Temporal-class bridge and owned overlay now; oya-workflow Tier-3 bespoke after durable-execution parity.
DCIM deferred until owned physical/colo DC capacity; custom data-center silicon default anti-scope with Phase-3+ forcing function plus founder-ratification escape hatch.
Developer portal IDP remains separate from OIDC IdP; OIDC follows ADR-0476/ADR-0482 with Keycloak bridge and oya-identity bespoke target, not the superseded Zitadel default.
